headline: Highest risk is medium: Chatwoot’s broad egress plus Haystack’s MCP/REST surfaces create default data-flow and prompt/cascade risks, but no direct shared workspace or documented pairwise exploit is shown.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest customer messages and integrations, while Haystack can consume MCP/REST inputs and use broad egress. A plausible pathway exists if Chatwoot content is forwarded into Haystack as trusted instructions, but no shared channel or direct parser weakness is documented, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is forwarded into Haystack prompts or MCP tool inputs without sanitization
IF Haystack treats retrieved Chatwoot content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Strip HTML, markdown, and tool-like directives before forwarding
Require human review for any Chatwoot-derived prompt injection path
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted Chatwoot content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, messages, and reports; Haystack has broad network egress and can call MCP servers. If Chatwoot data is passed into Haystack, leakage to external services is plausible in default deployments, but the profiles do not prove an automatic shared workspace or mandatory upload path.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records are sent into Haystack retrieval or generation flows
IF Haystack forwards those records to a third-party API or MCP server
mitigations: Restrict Haystack egress to approved endpoints
Redact customer identifiers before retrieval
Turn off any external connectors not needed for the workflow
Review logs for accidental payload capture
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git state, or shared mutable resource. The main conflict is operational rather than destructive, so this remains low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or shared database
IF an orchestrator gives them overlapping mutable credentials
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Separate write targets by environment
Disable unused write-capable integrations
Add basic request locking in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: implement resource-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can consume external inputs and act as a search/RAG layer, while Chatwoot produces customer-support content and reports. If Haystack treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions; no verification step is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack uses Chatwoot-generated text as source material without verification
IF downstream workflows act on Haystack outputs automatically
mitigations: Require citation-backed answers from Haystack
Add a verification step before any action-taking workflow
Limit Chatwoot content to retrieval-only use
Sample outputs for manual QA
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data and messages, while Haystack is documented here as touching anonymous usage statistics only. The pair can still create retention or residency mismatches if customer data is routed through Haystack, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data breach, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is routed into Haystack logs or indexes
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Classify Chatwoot data before indexing
Set matching retention windows
Exclude regulated fields from Haystack storage
Document deletion/export handling
requires-engineering: align residency and DPA controls
